Porto Grande/Mindelo Port (locode CVMIN) is Cape Verde's largest seaport located on Sao Vicente Island - one of the Barlavento Group's Cape Verde Islands. Sao Vicente is located between Santo Antao Island and Santa Luzia Island.

Mindelo Port (locode CVMIN) is usually visited by international cruise shipping companies whose vessels make stops during seasonal Transatlantic crossings between Europe and South America (RepositionCruises.com).

In January 2025, Port Mindelo joined the network (became under concession) of the world's largest cruise port operator Global Ports Holding/GPH.

In 2023, Cape Verde recorded 171 cruise ship calls and ~87,000 passengers. For 2024 were booked 250 berthings (estimated ~111,000 passengers).

Sao Vicente Island has a total population of around 80,000, land area of 227 km2 (88 mi2), length of 24 km (15 mi), width of 16 km (10 mi) and highest elevation point (Monte Verde) 725 m (2379 ft).

The island was discovered by the Portuguese in 1462, on St Vincent's Day (January 22nd) after who it is named. Due to the lack of fresh water, it was initially used only for grazing cattle by proprietors from the Santo Antao Island. Mindelo's natural harbor attracted pirates, which led to the building of a port fortification in 1734.

In 1838, in Porto Grande was established a coal deposit to supply Transatlantic ships on their crossing routes.

Sao Vicente was the first Cape Verde island to abolish slavery.

In 1874, telegraph lines (via Madeira Island) connected the island with Recife Brazil.

In the early 20th century, diesel ships started to replace steamships. The island's importance as a coal deposit port fell, and its economy declined.

As Sao Vicente lacks rain and natural resources, its current-day economy is mainly based on commerce and services.

There is an islet/small isle called Ilheu dos Passaros (north of Mindelo Bay), at ~2 km (1 mi) from the mainland.

Mindelo cruise terminal

Until 2024, cruise ships to Mindelo anchored off Porto Grande (on Sao Vicente Island's west-northern coast) and their passengers were transported/ferried ashore via the ship's tender boats.

In 2024 was completed the Mindelo Cruise Terminal. The modern facility features a large Quay (length 400 m/1312 ft) with max draft/water depth 11 m/36 ft allowing simultaneous berthing of two large vessels.

The Terminal's Welcome Building is sized 900 m2/9688 ft2 and has a Reception Hall and a separate part for administrative services.  The facility is also fitted with shore power equipment allowing docked ships to turn off their diesel engines and connect to the city's power grid, thus reducing noise and pollution.

The Mindelo Cruise Terminal project was co-funded by ORIO (financed by the Netherlands' Ministry of Foreign Affairs) and the OPEC Fund for International Development (1976-established by petroleum exporting countries finance institution).

Mindelo Cruise Terminal's development continued in 2025, adding a new 400-m/1312-ft-long jetty (to accommodate larger vessels), a Visitor Welcome Center, and a transportation hub. Dredging operations increased the Port's waterdepth, and Quay 9 (a former fishing quay) was rehabilitated for new functions. For the project was contracted a consortium led by Mota-Engil Group (a Portuguese company specializing in civil construction, public works, port operations, waste, water, and logistics) and Empreitel Figueiredo SA (building materials, civil engineering, building construction and project management consultant), with technical oversight from Artelia Group (France) and Grupo Norvia's Consultores de Engenharia SA (consultant).
